job.title: Systems Analyst | Insuretech | Amazing People
job.description:
• Salary range/guide: $90,000–120,000 pkg (inc. super)
  • Work type: Hybrid, 4 days on-site Tues–Fri / 1 day WFH (Mon)
  • Location: CBD, Sydney (harbour views)
  • Interview process: 2 stages (conversations)
  • Target start date: Any time after January 8th, 2027

Many analyst roles ask you to document what already exists.
This one asks you to configure it, test it and make it better.

Most analyst roles sit comfortably between meetings and templates. This one doesn’t.

You’ll work hands-on in the platform, configuring business rules and dynamic forms, investigating how systems behave, and finding where they could work smarter across an insurance and financial services platform.

Real exposure from day one.

Meaningful work, visible impact, and direct access to the people who make decisions.

What this role is (and isn’t)

This role is for someone who:

  • Asks why something works before suggesting how to fix it
  • Enjoys getting into the system itself: rules, forms, data and integrations
  • Can write for a developer and a business stakeholder on the same day
  • Wants to own outcomes, not just document them
  • Thrives with broad exposure in a flat, high-trust team

This role is probably not for someone who:

  • Prefers to stay on the business side and leave the technical details to others
  • Wants clearly defined swim lanes and a large team around them
  • Is looking for a tick-the-box, follow-the-process kind of role

The Work
You’ll sit at the intersection of business and technology, turning requirements into working configuration and making sure what gets built actually solves the problem. Practically, this means:

  1. Configuring and testing business rules in underwriting and claims rules engines
  2. Building and maintaining dynamic forms and reflexive questioning
  3. Translating requirements into functional specs, decision tables and data mappings
  4. Using SQL, APIs and JSON to investigate data, troubleshoot issues and find root causes
  5. Designing and running test scenarios with developers for rules, configuration and integrations

Example problems you might work on:

  1. Tracing why a claims rule is referring cases it shouldn’t, and fixing the logic.
  2. Reducing configuration time for new client implementations by separating what varies from what can be standardised.
  3. Mapping how insurance data flows between applications, underwriting, policy and claims, and where it breaks down.

None of these requires extensive years of experience. They require curiosity, structured thinking, and the willingness to dig in.

About You
You’re 1–3 years in as a Technical BA, Systems Analyst or similar, and you’re ready for real responsibility.
You bring:

  1. The ability to translate business needs into structured, implementable requirements
  2. Hands-on comfort with how information flows between systems, such as APIs, SQL, field mapping and config schemas
  3. Comfort working with rules logic, data definitions or validation criteria
  4. Strong analytical thinking and a habit of asking the right questions first before moving to solutions
  5. Exposure to AI tools or AI-assisted analysis and process improvement

Nice to have:

  1. Experience with Microsoft Azure or cloud platforms
  2. Familiarity with workflow automation, messaging systems or event-based architecture
  3. Any background in insurance, especially underwriting or claims (or a genuine willingness to learn)

What Excelling Looks Like

  • 3–6 months: You know the software and configuration tools well, and you’re contributing to configuration, testing and troubleshooting with less and less reliance on the technical team.
  • 6–9 months: You’re independently configuring and testing underwriting and claims rules, owning your deliverables, and building strong relationships with clients and the team.
  • 12 months: You’re a trusted, self-sufficient technical resource who challenges existing approaches and delivers measurable improvements.

You understand, not just do. That’s the bar.

About the Company
A highly successful Insurtech software company, operating for over 20 years, delivering sophisticated enterprise platforms used by financial and insurance organisations.

What makes them unique:

  • Stable, profitable business with an impressive enterprise client base
  • Boutique engineering environment with real ownership and influence
  • An unusually high average tenure of 12–15 years across the team

We quietly refer to them as the “unofficial employer of choice,” flying under the radar without ringing any bells.

Interview Process and Timelines
Our Solutions Architect will be on leave from 3rd to 18th December; therefore, ideally, we’re aiming to complete 1st-2nd interviews by Tues 1st Dec.

  • Stage 1: Video call with the COO and Solutions Architect
  • Stage 2: Interview with the CEO and other team members
  • Just real conversations about how you think, build and collaborate.

If this sounds like you
We’d love to hear from Systems Analysts and Technical BAs who are curious, take pride in their craft and want to take ownership.
After you apply, we’ll share the full job description and arrange a call shortly thereafter. We move fast, as does our client, and I mean lightning fast!

Questions?
Ramona - 02 9066 5512 | E: rjardin@3xpartners.com or
Craig - 0414 959 608 | E: cbagshaw@3xpartners.com

Note:
Applications are reviewed outside of normal business hours (inc. weekends). Initial contact is typically via email.

If shortlisted, you’ll receive an invitation to our digital portal: noreply@perpetualhire.com

job.title: Quant/Developer- C#, .NET, Azure
job.description:
Most quant developers inherit a library. This role lets you rebuild them.
Our client is an established investment manager. Their quant/dev team is rebuilding its core libraries for the cloud, and they want you to help shape what comes next.

Why this role is different

  1. You’ll build, not just maintain. You’ll rewrite the core quant libraries as they move from on-prem to Azure.
  2. You’ll sit with the business. You’ll work directly with quants and portfolio managers, not in a separate dev team that only sees tickets.
  3. You’ll do work that builds your career. A full library rebuild and cloud move doesn’t come along often.
  4. You’ll learn from a respected leader. The team is led by a highly regarded quant leader.

What your days will look like

  1. Writing C#.NET on the quant desk, focused on fixed income
  2. Taking existing libraries apart and rethinking how they should work
  3. Working with the people who use your code, so you understand why it matters, not just how to build it

You’ll feel at home here if you…

  1. Are a strong C#.NET developer who has worked on or alongside a quant desk
  2. Understand fixed income, especially vanilla bonds, and can talk about yield curves
  3. Would rather understand the business than just close tickets
  4. Bonus points for Python, Java, JavaScript, and Azure or other cloud experience

The details

  1. Permanent, full-time
  2. Sydney CBD, with 3 days in the office
  3. $200-220K guide + bonus
